title: Dizzy a week after COVID-19

source.citation: Waleed MS, Dhulipalla L, Niazi M, et al. COVID-Induced Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura: A Case Report and Treatment-Focused Review. Cureus. 2024;16(3):e57252.

presentation.chiefComplaint: Dizziness and lightheadedness since this morning
presentation.hpi: Dizziness and lightheadedness since earlier today. A week ago urgent care diagnosed COVID-19 after headaches and weakness. On the way to hospital her right arm went numb; in the ED she feels better and the numbness has gone.

diagnosis.primary: Immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura after COVID-19 (ADAMTS13 activity <2% with an inhibitor)

management: Two units of packed red cells in the ED
Prednisone 1 mg/kg daily and therapeutic plasma exchange from the next morning (four sessions, days 2, 3, 4 and 7)
Rituximab a few days after admission
outcome: LDH fell from 930 to 500 U/L and ADAMTS13 activity recovered to 41.7%; platelets were 649 x10³/µL before discharge.
teachingPoints: Thrombocytopenia plus microangiopathic hemolysis (schistocytes, high LDH, low haptoglobin) is TTP until proven otherwise; neurological symptoms may be transient.
A PLASMIC score of 6–7 predicts severe ADAMTS13 deficiency, so treatment starts before the result is back.
Start plasma exchange and corticosteroids urgently and avoid platelet transfusion unless bleeding is life-threatening; rituximab and caplacizumab are added in immune TTP (ISTH 2020).

questions.q: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.extra: Hemoglobin 5.7 g/dL, platelets 69 x10³/µL, LDH 930 U/L, low haptoglobin, mildly raised bilirubin, acute kidney injury. Blood film: 4–5 schistocytes per high-power field. CT head: no acute pathology.
questions.explanation: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (schistocytes, LDH 930 U/L, low haptoglobin) with thrombocytopenia and a transient neurological deficit is thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura until proven otherwise; ADAMTS13 activity was <2% with an inhibitor. Immune thrombocytopenia does not hemolyze, and the stool was brown.

questions.q: Her PLASMIC score is 6. What does this mean?
options: High probability of severe ADAMTS13 deficiency
Low probability, so look for another cause
questions.explanation: The PLASMIC score (platelets <30, hemolysis, no active cancer, no transplant, MCV <90 fL, INR <1.5, creatinine <2.0 mg/dL; one point each) predicts severe ADAMTS13 deficiency: 6–7 is high risk, so treatment starts before the ADAMTS13 result returns.

questions.q: Which treatment should start as soon as possible?
questions.explanation: Immune TTP is a hematological emergency: daily plasma exchange (removes the ADAMTS13 inhibitor and replaces the enzyme) with corticosteroids, plus rituximab and, where available, caplacizumab (ISTH 2020 guidelines). Platelet transfusion is avoided unless bleeding is life-threatening.

evidence.quote: A 51-year-old female with a past medical history of hypertension
presented to the emergency department (ED) with a complaint of dizziness and lightheadedness that started earlier in the day
She had recently visited urgent care for headaches and weakness and was diagnosed with COVID-19 a week ago.
On her way to the hospital, she had right arm numbness.
In the ED, the patient said she felt better and denied any numbness in the right arm.
She was afebrile, had a blood pressure of 183/91 mmHg, and a heart rate of 120 beats per minute.
Her hemoglobin being 5.7 g/dL, she was given two units of packed red blood cells (PRBC) in the ED
LDH trended down from 930 units/L to 500 units/L.
acute kidney injury, low haptoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) over 900 U/L, mildly elevated total bilirubin
four to five schistocytes per high power field (HPF)
ADAMTS13 activity of <2%, and ADAMTS13 antibody of 21 units/mL were noted.
CT head showed no acute pathology
The patient started on steroids (1 mg/kg prednisone) daily the next morning.
The patient was started on therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) the next morning.
After four sessions of TPE (Days 2, 3, 4, and 7 of admission), ADAMTS-13 activity improved to 41.7%.
We also started our patient on rituximab a few days after her admission and post-plasmapheresis.
The platelet count remained stable and was 649K/uL before discharge.
